question.text: The tangent to the curve $y=e^x$ drawn at the point $\left(c, e^c\right)$ intersects the line joining the points $\left(c-1, e^{c-1}\right)$ and $\left(c+1, e^{c+1}\right)$

solution.text:
Slope of the line joining the points $\left(c-1, e^{c-1}\right)$ and $\left(c+1, e^{c+1}\right)$ is equal to $\frac{e^{c+1}-e^{c-1}}{2}>e^c$
$$ \text { Tangent to the curve } y=e^x \text { will intersect the given line to the left of the line } x=c \text {. } $$ ALITER The equation of the tangent to the curve $y=e^x$ at $\left(c, e^c\right)$ is $$ y-e^c=e^c(x-c) $$ Equation of the line joining the given points is $$ y-e^{c-1}=\frac{e^c\left(e-e^{-1}\right)}{2}[x-(c-1)] $$ Eliminating $y$ from Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $$ \begin{aligned} {[x-(c-1)]\left[2-\left(e-e^{-1}\right)\right] } & =2 e^{-1} \\ x-c & =\frac{e+e^{-1}-2}{2-\left(e-e^{-1}\right)} < 0 \Rightarrow x < c . \end{aligned} $$
